# seqout

> seqout is a search engine for public sequencing datasets. It unifies metadata from NCBI GEO, SRA, ENA, DDBJ (DRA and GEA), EBI ArrayExpress and GSA into a single relevance-ranked search, with consolidated sample tables, cross-archive cross-references, similarity graphs, download links, and SLM-enriched ontology metadata (tissue, cell type, disease). Built at Saket Lab, IIT Bombay.

Coverage is roughly 1M projects and studies (GEO Series, SRA/ENA/DDBJ studies,
ArrayExpress experiments) and tens of millions of samples, experiments and runs,
across NCBI GEO, NCBI SRA, EBI ENA, DDBJ (DRA and GEA), EBI ArrayExpress, GSA and
BioProject, with publication links carrying journal and citation counts.

Search is at https://seqout.org/search?q={query}. Every record has a stable URL:
a project at https://seqout.org/p/{accession} (for example /p/GSE196830,
/p/SRP123456, /p/E-MTAB-1234), a sample at https://seqout.org/s/{accession}, an
experiment at https://seqout.org/e/{accession}, a run at
https://seqout.org/r/{accession}, an author at https://seqout.org/authors/{name},
a publication at https://seqout.org/pmid/{pmid}, and every study filed under one
submission at https://seqout.org/submission/{accession}.

The same data is available over a REST API at https://seqout.org/api and over MCP at
https://seqout.org/api/mcp, which exposes search, project and sample metadata,
download manifests and enriched metadata as tools.

The Python and R clients search the same data, resolve an accession to its records in
every archive, and read GEO supplementary files as counts matrices.

```bash
uv add seqout                    # Python library, needs Python 3.13+
uv add 'seqout[counts]'          # with the counts-matrix readers
uv tool install seqout           # the seqout command line
```

```r
pak::pak("saketlab/seqout/R")
install.packages("seqout", repos = "https://saketlab.r-universe.dev")
```

```python
from seqout import connect, seqout_counts

sq = connect()
sq.search("liver cancer scRNA", organism="Homo sapiens")
sq.get("GSE151530").samples
seqout_counts(gse="GSE297547").matrix(sample="GSM8994520")
```

```r
library(seqout)

SeqoutSearch("liver cancer scRNA", organism = "Homo sapiens")
SeqoutGet("GSE151530")$samples
Seqout2Seurat("GSE297547", sample = "GSM8994520")
```

Every project page ends with ready-to-run Python and R code for that accession,
and https://seqout.org/p/{accession} returns it as markdown when requested with
`Accept: text/markdown`.

seqout is developed and maintained by Saket Lab, IIT Bombay.

## Docs

- [Search](https://seqout.org/search): relevance-ranked search across every archive
- [Find projects by author](https://seqout.org/authors): every dataset a named researcher authored
- [Find projects by PMID](https://seqout.org/pmid): every dataset linked to a PubMed ID
- [Dataset map](https://seqout.org/map): where in the world the data was submitted from
- [Statistics](https://seqout.org/stats): growth by archive, organism, platform and country
- [Data downloads](https://seqout.org/data): the whole database as Parquet, for DuckDB or the CLI
- [FAQ](https://seqout.org/faq): what seqout indexes, how often it updates, and what it is for
- [How search works](https://seqout.org/howsearchworks): ranking, filters and query syntax
- [API reference](https://seqout.org/api-docs): every REST endpoint, with parameters and examples
- [MCP server](https://seqout.org/mcp): setup for Claude Desktop and other LLM agents

## Clients

- [Overview](https://seqout.org/cli/): both clients, install commands and a worked example
- [Python library and CLI](https://seqout.org/cli/python/): `connect()`, `Dataset`, and the `seqout` command
- [R package](https://seqout.org/cli/R/): reference index and articles
- [Client llms.txt](https://seqout.org/cli/llms.txt): index of the client documentation
- [Client llms-full.txt](https://seqout.org/cli/llms-full.txt): all of it inlined, including the full API reference

## Optional

- [llms-full.txt](https://seqout.org/llms-full.txt): this index with the FAQ, search guide and API reference inlined
- [Saket Lab](https://saketlab.org): the group that builds and maintains seqout
- [Web source](https://github.com/saketlab/seqout-web): the seqout.org front end
- [Client source](https://github.com/saketlab/seqout): the Python and R clients, MIT licensed
